rooms.5700: A forecourt of raked white gravel lies before the Academy, edged with clipped box hedges and two stone urns of rosemary. The Eastern Gatehouse stands a short way to the north, its lanterns pale in the daylight, and the murmur of the Trade Road drifts from it. To the south a flight of shallow marble steps rises to bronze-banded doors left open to the morning. Carved across the lintel in letters a hand deep is a single word.
rooms.5701: You stand in the vestibule of the Academy, a long hall of cool grey marble where every footstep rings. Niches in the walls hold busts of bearded thinkers, their noses polished smooth by generations of hopeful hands. Doors open north upon the forecourt, and the hall runs east and west into the wings. To the south an arch frames the garden, a green glow beyond it.
rooms.5716: A broad corridor runs the length of the North Wing, its floor laid in black and white squares like a board for some patient game. Tall windows of thick greenish glass admit a watery light, and between them hang tapestries of the Seven Sages, their threads gone dull. A rack of scroll cases leans against the wall, each labelled in a cramped scholarly hand. The passage ends east at a corner, and west it opens toward the vestibule.
rooms.5715: Two corridors meet at the Northeast Corner in a square little hall under a ribbed ceiling painted midnight blue and scattered with gilt stars. A bronze astrolabe the size of a cartwheel is bolted to the wall, its rings still turning at a touch. A cushioned bench waits in the angle for those who must think before they go on. The way south leads down the East Wing, and the North Wing runs back west.
rooms.5714: The East Wing is panelled in dark oak to the height of a man, with brass lamps burning in brackets at every third pace. A smell of beeswax and old vellum hangs in the air. A heavy door stands open to the east upon the Lecture Room on Logic, and the scrape of chalk on slate comes faintly through it. The corridor runs on south and turns back north toward the corner.

5722.description: Rising tiers of oak benches face a lectern and a great slate wall covered in chalked syllogisms, half rubbed out and rewritten in another hand. Each bench has an inkwell sunk in its arm, and a few quills lie where they were dropped. Behind the lectern a trapdoor of iron-studded planks stands ajar upon a steep stair that leads down to the Paradox Closet. The only other way out is west, to the East Wing.

rooms.5732: This cramped closet holds nothing but shelves of locked boxes, each labelled This Box Is Empty and each heavy when lifted. A card pinned over the door says Do Not Read This Card. The air is close and smells of lamp oil and dust. A stair climbs up to the Lecture Room on Logic, and a door in the far wall leads south to a gloomier chamber.
rooms.5733: A low windowless room lit by a single swinging lamp, whose shadow never seems to fall where it should. The same sentence is painted across the walls in a dozen hands, All that is written here is false, and under each someone has scrawled a furious rebuttal. Three-legged stools stand round a table scarred with knife-points. A door north returns to the Paradox Closet, and another south leads on.
rooms.5734: The ceiling of this long narrow chamber is hung with hundreds of painted wooden arrows, each dangling on a thread and none ever seen to land. At the end of the room a target of straw and canvas waits, always a little farther off than it was. Dust lies thick on the boards where no one has ever got across. The Liar's Den lies back north, and the room opens south onto a running track.
rooms.5735: A running track of packed sand, ringed by a low wall, has been laid out beneath an oval vault of whitewashed brick. Two sets of footprints are pressed into it, one far ahead of the other, and neither pair seems to have made any progress. A stone tortoise squats at the starting line, polished smooth by passing palms. A door east returns to the Paradox Closet, and the track bends south.
rooms.5736: The track goes on and on between low whitewashed walls hung with faded pennants. Every few strides a marble post is numbered with a fraction, one half, three quarters, seven eighths, each nearer the next than the last. The sand is scuffed into long grooves by feet that never quite arrive. Behind you the track runs back north to the starting line, and ahead it looks exactly as it did before.
rooms.5713: Round arches open on the west side of the East Wing, giving long views into the garden, where green leaves nod in a draught from nowhere. The inner wall is hung with framed maps of lands the Academy's masters have never visited, drawn from other men's reports. A brass drinking fountain gurgles in a niche, its basin stained green. The corridor runs north and south, and a gap in the arches leads west into the garden.
rooms.5712: Here the East Wing grows narrower and the lamps burn brighter, as if the Sophists wished their listeners to see every smile. Dried rose petals lie swept into drifts along the skirting. A curtained archway to the east opens into the lecture room on Sophism, where silver tongues are trained. The passage runs north toward the garden arches and south to the corner.
rooms.5721: A theatre in miniature: a curved dais of polished cedar faces a semicircle of cushioned couches, with a gilded chair at its centre for whoever is to be persuaded. Painted on the dome overhead are Gorgias, Protagoras and their pupils, gesturing with enviable ease. Lamps on tall tripods give a flattering honeyed light. A pitcher of wine stands stale on the speaker's table, and the only way out is west to the East Wing.
rooms.5711: In the Southeast Corner a window seat looks down through narrow panes on a kitchen yard heaped with cabbage stalks and broken amphorae. The plaster is patched here and the paint is older than that of the lecture halls, a sign that the Academy's wealth thins toward the servants' end. A brazier warms the angle against the draught. The passage leads north along the East Wing and west into the South Wing.
rooms.5710: The South Wing is plainer than the others, its floor of worn flagstones and its walls limewashed, with iron hooks at intervals for lanterns and coats. A low door in the south wall has a rope handle in place of a latch, and from behind it comes the smell of boiled barley and wet wool. The corridor stretches west toward the middle of the wing and east to the corner. The door south leads to the Slave Quarters.
rooms.5720: Rows of narrow plank bunks with straw pallets fill the long low room, each with a peg above it holding one spare tunic. There is no window, only a grating high in the wall that lets in a smear of grey light and the smell of the kitchen. Names are scratched into the beams, some many times over, some only once. A single door leads back north to the South Wing.
rooms.5709: Midway along the South Wing an open archway looks north upon the garden, where a white pavilion shows pale among the trees. A long runner of threadbare carpet leads on, and a row of benches faces the wall as if their sitters were waiting for a summons that never came. A clock of water and brass drips patiently in a niche, marking hours no one keeps. East and west the passage goes on along the wing.
rooms.5725: Gravel paths cross here beneath a trellis of climbing roses that has outgrown its frame and tumbled into the beds. A marble pavilion stands north, its columns wreathed in ivy, and the path to it is worn pale by feet. An arch in the wall to the south leads back into the South Wing. Overhead the leaded glass of the roof is streaked and green, and the air beneath it is damp and warm and smells of loam.
rooms.5765: Eight slender columns hold up a domed roof of white marble, and the floor is a mosaic of interlocking squares in cream and rose. At the centre a round stone cover the width of a cartwheel has been set into the floor, ringed with brass and furrowed by chains. Beneath it a stair plunges down into dankness, and a warm sour breath rises from it. The garden lies south, bright and green, but the pavilion itself feels watched.

5750.description: The stair ends in a low brick chamber where several passages begin at once and none looks different from another. Water beads the walls, and the air is thick, warm and faintly sweet, like meat left too long in a larder. A chalked arrow on the floor has been scuffed out and redrawn so many times that it points at nothing. The steps behind you are lost already in the gloom.

5752.description: Rusted rings are set in the walls of this junction, as though something was once tethered here, and the brick beneath them is scored with long grooves. A narrow ladder of iron staples climbs into a black slot overhead, and another drops into a hole in the floor. Passages leave in every direction, and all of them smell the same: wet clay, lamp soot and something sweetly rotten.

5751.description: The walls here are daubed with white paint in looping symbols that might be a mathematician's despair or a lost student's last attempt at a map. A rope hangs from a hatch in the ceiling, frayed at the end where it was cut. A drain in the floor gurgles and breathes out warm air. Every turning looks like the one before it.

5753.description: A round chamber with a domed ceiling of small bricks, where a dry whisper returns your own footsteps a moment late and slightly altered. Broken crockery lies in a ring on the floor, bowls and cups pitched against the wall in some old tantrum. A hole in the floor shows a dim glow far below, and a ladder of staples climbs into the dome above.

5754.description: The passage narrows to a throat barely wide enough for a man's shoulders, the bricks bulging inward as if something enormous pressed on them from the far side. A stair of worn wedge-shaped steps climbs one way and another descends the other. Scratches at the height of a hand cover the stone, thousands of them, in groups of five. The smell is stronger here.

5755.description: Lamp brackets in the walls hold stubs of tallow candles burned down to puddles, the remains of an expedition that lit its way and still lost it. A bent iron grate lies in a corner with a bundle of mouldering rags beside it. A cramped stair spirals up toward a small niche, and another spiral drops away below. The air feels thick, as if it had been breathed many times.

5756.description: Raised on a plinth in the middle of this chamber is a stone bust of a man with his eyes gouged out and his mouth stopped with clay. A gutter circles the plinth and carries a thin dark trickle into a hole to one side. Steps lead down into a lower passage. The walls sweat, and green-black stains creep from the floor to the ceiling.

5757.description: The brickwork gives way here to a stretch of smooth black stone, as though a different hand built this corner of the maze. In the wall to the east a panel the width of a door, edged with a hairline seam, stands slightly proud of the stone. A handprint in the dust beside it shows where someone has often pushed it open. Passages continue in other directions, and stairs lead both up and down.

rooms.5764: This cramped closet behind the panel is narrow as a wardrobe, its walls lined with shelves of stoppered jars whose labels have faded to brown ghosts. A sheet of sketches pinned to the plaster shows a creature drawn again and again, each version a little less like anything alive. The panel swings shut behind you with a soft click and a sigh of mortar dust. The air is stale and tastes of vinegar.

5758.description: Bones of small animals, rats and cats and one that might have been a dog, lie in drifts along the foot of the walls, picked clean and set in neat rows. A net of dark wire sags from the ceiling, torn through in the middle. The roof is low enough to brush your hair, and a narrow stair rises into the dark overhead. Something has been collecting here, and carefully.

5759.description: The maze loosens its grip a little here: the floor is swept, and a brass lamp with a clean wick burns in a bracket at the head of a short flight of steps. Long streaks on the brick show where something heavy has been dragged in and out. A lit landing to the north promises order, and the stench thins as you near it. Passages lead off on every other hand.

rooms.5760: A small stone landing, swept and lamp-lit, lies before a door of black walnut bound with silver. A mat of woven reed is laid at the threshold, and above the lintel hangs a brass plate engraved with a name and a short warning to visitors. Dust has been brushed from the handle by a hand that comes often. The door stands east, and the maze closes in again to the north, west and south.
rooms.5761: Books climb to the ceiling in crooked towers, and every flat surface bears a clutter of astrolabes, retorts, bell jars and loose pages crawling with equations. A great desk of dark wood sits under a lamp of green glass, an open journal upon it in a hurried hand. Glass tanks along one wall hold pale pickled shapes that were never quite natural. The only way out is west, back to the landing.
rooms.5762: A hole barely large enough to crouch in has been scraped from the brick and lined with sacking. A candle stub sits in a saucer beside a clay cup, and chalk marks on the wall count days in fives, then stop. A low door of planks leads west, and a spiral stair drops back down into the maze. The air here is a little cleaner, and someone has tried to keep it so.
rooms.5763: A tidy tiny chamber, arranged by someone who refused to go mad. A narrow cot is made up with a folded blanket, a shelf holds a few salvaged books, and a ledger on an upturned crate logs the days in a steady hand. Chalked proofs cover one wall beside a map of the maze with many corrections. The only way out is east, to the niche.
rooms.5730: A low wall along one side of this corner of the garden carries pear trees trained flat against the stone, their fruit hard and green. A stone bench sits in the angle with a cushion of moss on one arm. Gravel crunches underfoot, and a path leads north toward a sundial and west toward the roses. Rain has never fallen here, yet the leaves always glisten.
rooms.5724: A bronze sundial on a fluted pedestal stands at the meeting of four paths, though no sun reaches it beneath the glass, and the gnomon casts only a smudge of shadow. Arches in the wall to the east open into the East Wing. Paths lead north to the vines, south to a corner of pear trees, and west to the fountain. Lavender borders the gravel and scents the damp air.
rooms.5729: A grape arbour covers this corner of the garden, its vines trained over a frame of white-painted iron until the leaves meet overhead in a green tunnel. Bunches of small black fruit hang just out of reach. A stone seat inside holds a sunken cushion and a forgotten volume of verse. Paths run south toward the sundial and west along the far beds.
rooms.5723: The garden begins here at the foot of an arch from the vestibule, where an olive tree grows from a great clay tub and its silver leaves tremble in the warm air. Box hedges are clipped into squares and spirals, and gravel walks lead off between them. A low stone plaque set in the path reads Nothing In Excess. The way north returns to the Northern Side of the Academy, and paths wind east, south and west.
rooms.5727: A round fountain stands at the heart of the garden, its basin of grey marble carved with leaping fish, though the spout has run dry and only the mist of condensed air drips from the rim. Four paths meet at the basin, each edged with trimmed hedges. Benches sit round it at even intervals, as if for a conversation long ended. Paths lead north, east and west from here.
rooms.5726: Raised herb beds of thyme, sage and bitter wormwood fill this part of the garden, each labelled on a slate tablet in neat chalk. A rain barrel of cracked oak stands under a drainpipe and hums with a faint insect drone. The scent of crushed leaves hangs in the damp air. A broad arch in the wall to the west leads into the West Wing, and paths run north, east and south.
rooms.5728: A single great pear tree, the oldest in the garden, spreads over a ring of seats made from sawn logs, where disputations were once held. Its fruit lies rotting in the grass in a sweet brown drift. The lattice of the glass roof shows green with moss, and the light that gets through it is dim and speckled. The path leads east and south.
rooms.5731: A small lily pond lies here, its stone rim worn into hollows by sitting and its water dark as tea, with a few pale blossoms floating at the edges. Moss has crept over the flagstones, and the air is thick with the scent of damp earth. A path leads north toward the herb beds and east toward the roses and a white pavilion.
rooms.5705: The West Wing here is lined with doors of dark oak, each with a brass plate engraved with the name of a master long dead. Long windows of rippled glass throw wavering light across the floor. At the foot of the wall a runner of faded red wool absorbs every step. The passage runs north and south along the wing, and an arch on the east side opens onto the garden.
rooms.5704: The corridor widens into a bay at the foot of a little flight of steps. A heavy door to the west stands open on the lecture room of Heraclitus, and the faint sound of running water drifts from it. Pegs along the wall hold dusty academic gowns of grey and brown. The West Wing runs south from here, and the corner lies north.
rooms.5703: The Northwest Corner is a round chamber with a domed ceiling pierced by a lantern of coloured glass, which throws wandering rainbows on the floor. A circular bench runs round the walls, and in the middle stands a small table with a chessboard, its pieces locked in mid-argument. A draught moves the dust. Corridors lead east along the North Wing and south down the West Wing.
rooms.5702: Portraits of former heads of the Academy hang along this stretch of the North Wing in gilt frames, each more severe than the last. Between them narrow shelves hold rolled maps tied with faded ribbon. The floor is worn into two shallow troughs by the passage of countless feet. The vestibule lies east, and the corner opens west.
rooms.5717: A shallow stone channel runs round the floor of this lecture room, fed by a trickle from a spout in the wall, so that the sound of flowing water is never absent. At the lectern a brazier of iron burns with a low red flame fed by pitch. On the wall behind it, painted in tall black letters, stands a saying about rivers and fire. Only one door leads out, east to the West Wing.
rooms.5706: A smell of woodsmoke and cabbage broth drifts along this stretch of the West Wing from the kitchens beyond the walls. The plaster is yellow with age, and a row of pegs holds nothing but a single forgotten scarf. A stained board announces the hours of the lectures in a faded hand. To the west a door stands ajar on the lecture room on Stoicism, and the wing runs north and south.
rooms.5707: The Southwest Corner is a dim, narrow place where two wings meet and neither has much to say. A small window of greenish glass looks out on a walled yard of firewood. A chipped bust of Zeno sits on a shelf, his nose long since broken off. Passages lead north along the West Wing and east along the South Wing.
rooms.5708: The South Wing is wider here, with a vaulted ceiling hung with lamps of tarnished brass and a smell of roast meat in the air. A pair of double doors to the south stands open on the dining hall, from which comes the clink of pewter. Rush matting lines the floor. The corridor leads west to the corner and east along the wing.
rooms.5719: A long hall of scrubbed oak tables and plain benches stretches under a ceiling of dark beams, where lamps hang on chains. A great hearth fills the end wall, its fire banked to embers beneath a spit and a row of iron pots. Carved on the mantel are the names of every master since the founding. Trestles stand stacked against the wall, and the only door is north to the South Wing.
rooms.5718: A bare room of whitewashed walls and a plain stone floor, without a single ornament, for the Stoics held that comfort was a distraction. Rows of backless benches face a low platform, and over its edge hangs a coarse woollen curtain. Painted on the wall is a porch of columns, as though to remind pupils of the school's origin. The only way out is east, to the West Wing.

5700.description: The word is Inquire, cut deep and gilded once, the gilt now mostly worn to a few bright flecks.

5732.description: The card is written in a beautiful hand, and it is quite impossible to read it without breaking its rule.

5756.description: The bust is of Phaeton himself, to judge by the heavy brow and the proud chin. Someone has taken a chisel to the eyes.

5717.description: The saying is that no man steps twice into the same river, for it is not the same river and he is not the same man.

5761.description: The last entries are cramped and damp-stained, recording an experiment that was to join the wisdom of many minds in a single body. The final line says only that it has outgrown its cage.

5723.description: The plaque is old, and the lettering has been worn nearly smooth by feet.

creatures.long_desc: A pale scholar in a grey gown stands muttering over a scroll.
creatures.description: He is thin and ink-fingered, with the unhealthy pallor of one who reads by lamplight. A leather satchel of scrolls hangs at his hip, and he looks up at strangers with absent, patient annoyance.

creatures.long_desc: A weary slave in a rough tunic goes about his chores with lowered eyes.
creatures.description: A lean, stooped man with a brand on his forearm and rope-calloused hands. He keeps his gaze on the floor and moves as if every footstep were measured against a lash.

creatures.long_desc: A giant maze rat the size of a hound scuttles along the wall with its yellow teeth bared.
creatures.description: Its fur is sleek, almost glossy, and its eyes are the wrong colour, a flat and thoughtful green. It moves along the passages as if it knew them very well.

creatures.long_desc: A towering bronze golem stands guard, its green-veined joints creaking with each slow breath of steam.
creatures.description: The golem is twice the height of a man, cast in the likeness of a bearded sage with a hammer for a hand. Verdigris crusts its seams, and a thin steam escapes from a vent in its back with a faint hissing wheeze.

creatures.long_desc: An arch sophist in silk robes stands upon the dais, smiling the smile of a man who has never lost an argument.
creatures.description: He is handsome and sleek, with oiled curls and rings on every finger, and a voice like warm honey. His eyes, though, are quite cold, and they measure you for the price of your purse.

creatures.long_desc: Aporia the failed experiment lurches through the passage, a patchwork thing of many mismatched limbs.
creatures.description: A sprawling heap of flesh and hide stitched together from a dozen creatures, scholar, hound and ox, it drags a trailing arm and murmurs half-remembered syllogisms in a dozen voices. Its eyes are set in the wrong places and all of them are weeping.

creatures.long_desc: Phaeton, master of the Academy, bends over his desk with ink on his cuffs and madness in his eyes.
creatures.description: A tall gaunt man in a threadbare black gown, with a hawk's nose and white hair standing in tufts. He mutters in Greek and in numbers, and a staff of pale ash glows faintly in his fist. The brilliance in his eyes has long since curdled into something else.

items.room_desc: A pointed bronze stylus lies here.
items.description: A scribe's stylus of bronze, long and sharp, with a flattened end for scraping out mistakes. It will serve as a dagger in a pinch.

items.room_desc: A honeyed barley cake sits here, wrapped in a cloth.
items.description: A dense little cake of barley meal sweetened with dark honey, baked in the Academy's kitchens.

items.room_desc: A greenish bronze breastplate lies here.
items.description: A piece torn from a golem's chest, heavy, green with verdigris and engraved with tiny rows of numbers. Hammered into a fit, it makes a stout cuirass.

items.room_desc: A silver ring set with a polished stone lies here.
items.description: A silver band whose inner side is inscribed with a very small, very clever argument. The wearer feels a little sharper in the head.

items.room_desc: A cloak of stitched and knotted hide lies here.
items.description: A cloak stitched from many hides of different animals, tough and ill-smelling, with a knot at the clasp that no hand can untie.

items.room_desc: A pale ash staff, faintly warm to the eye, lies here.
items.description: A staff of pale ash, carved with spiralling equations from foot to crown. It hums gently when swung, and the wood is faintly warm.
